summary: IMPLEMENTED: python -B -m dev_supervisor (cli.py, __main__.py) with start, status, workers, assign, handoff, compact-check, replace, report, snapshot, route, doctor and config. Each is non-destructive without --yes and exits non-zero on a failed check (1 failed/refused, 2 usage/config, compact-check 3 pressure UNAVAILABLE, 4 COMPACT/REPLACE due). It integrates L1-L7 without re-implementing them: L1 telemetry/evidence, L2 StateStore/WorkerRegistry/Supervisor/ClaudeCliLauncher (worker permission mode added by overriding Supervisor.build_spec, still built by build_claude_argv), L3 build/write/verify_handoff, compaction.decide and replace_session, L4 routing.decide and OmniRouteClient, L5 resolve_discovery.discover, L6 GitHubLogger (events are spooled by the loop and posted only by report --yes), and L7 build_snapshot. config.py: a machine-local config (default <state dir>/config.json or CREATORSTUDIO_DEV_SUPERVISOR_CONFIG, refused inside a git tree). It covers models, context windows, thresholds, OmniRoute URL, GitHub repo/issue, allow_paid_api=false and dangerously_skip_permissions=false. Credential-like keys or values are refused. The template has placeholders only (docstring and `config --example`). launch.py DECISION, resolving the open point from L3: Main is an INTERACTIVE claude session in a new console window (subprocess.Popen with an argument list, CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE, shell=False, no cmd/wt string parsing, .cmd/.bat shims refused, cwd = repo root). Its argv is --model, --session-id <uuid>, --name, --append-system-prompt-file <state dir>/prompts/main-<uuid>.prompt.txt (operating instructions plus the verified handoff path and hash after a replacement), an optional --permission-mode, and --dangerously-skip-permissions only when the config enables it. Workers stay headless via L2. InteractiveMainLauncher implements the L2 ProcessLauncher protocol so L3 replace_session relaunches Main interactively. LIMITS: the supervisor observes Main only through the L1 session file and transcript tail and cannot inject keystrokes. Compacting an interactive Main therefore means Main writes a handoff, the supervisor verifies it by read-back, then replaces the session (auto only when auto_replace_main=true, the session is idle and a handoff written within 30 min verifies). An old Main this process did not start is never signalled; the result is REPLACED_OLD_NOT_CLEARED and the user closes the window. CLI commands never write the worker registry while a loop runs: assign/replace --yes queue requests in <state>/requests and the loop holding the lock executes them. The provider (Claude Pro vs OmniRoute) is inherited from whichever local launcher opened the terminal. The supervisor never reads, copies or edits pro.ps1, backup.ps1 or .mcp.json (none were read in this lane). OBSERVED live (once, bounded, haiku, temp state dir and temp git repo outside the repository, no repository writes): the L2 worker path ran end to end. Argv: ["claude","-p","--output-format","stream-json","--verbose","--model","haiku","--session-id","<uuid>"], prompt on stdin. Result: exit 0 in 8.5 s, worker status EXITED, 4 stream lines with event types system/init, assistant, rate_limit_event, result/success, is_error false, num_turns 1, result session_id equal to --session-id, result text exactly 'OK', stderr 0 bytes. This PROVES the L2 assumptions that -p reads the prompt from stdin and that stream-json needs --verbose (without --verbose: exit 1 in 2 s, 'Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose'). --append-system-prompt-file is not listed in `claude --help` (2.1.316) but was OBSERVED accepted (claude -p --model haiku --append-system-prompt-file <tmp>: exit 0, output 'OK'; control: an unknown option gives 'error: unknown option', exit 1). Doctor and the read-only commands were run against the real machine (see commands). NOT TESTED: the interactive Main launch (NewConsoleTerminal) and a real replacement or retirement of an interactive Main were never run live; start --yes was not run on this machine; report --yes was not run live (no real posting); the Resolve MCP transport is not wired (L5 has none); the session-file heartbeat on a real interactive session is unobserved; non-Windows interactive launch is not implemented. Nothing is VERIFIED.

Add an owner entry for 'orchestrator/dev_supervisor/' (and the test_dev_*.py files) in the registry that test reads. Not edited here (registry off limits).

No change to any L2-owned file is required: the live check confirmed the L2 launcher assumptions (-p reads stdin; stream-json requires --verbose). Note for L2/L1: the stream contains a 'rate_limit_event' event type that neither lane parses yet. It may be an account-usage source for L1 (shape not inspected, so NOT TESTED).

L2 Supervisor.build_spec does not pass a permission mode, so a headless worker with no --permission-mode gets tool calls that need approval denied. L8 adds worker_permission_mode through a subclass (ConfiguredSupervisor). Whether workers should default to acceptEdits is an OPEN decision for Lukas (default here: none).

NOT TESTED live: the interactive Main launch in a new console (CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE), the session-file heartbeat of an interactive session, an interactive replacement and retirement, start --yes, report --yes, replace --yes. The first real `python -B -m dev_supervisor start --yes` should be observed by the integrator or Lukas.
Interactive Main is Windows-only (NewConsoleTerminal refuses other platforms); a POSIX terminal strategy is not designed.
Retiring an interactive Main started by an earlier supervisor process is manual (the user closes the old window); the supervisor never signals a pid it did not start.
The decision (interactive Main, headless workers, compaction = verified handoff then replacement) should be recorded by L9/Coordinator in the docs; L8 records it only in launch.py and this report.
